hints.title: Cyclic Node Duplication Obstacle
hints.text: Graphs can contain cycles and multiple paths to the same vertex. When creating copies of vertices and edges, how can you prevent infinite recursion while preserving the original topology and vertex values?

hints.title: Original-to-Clone Map Invariant
hints.text: A lookup registry mapping original vertices to their freshly allocated counterparts guarantees each vertex is cloned only once and shared edges are correctly reconstructed.

hints.title: Recursive Node Cloning Procedure
hints.text: Return null if the input vertex is null. Check if the vertex already exists in a lookup table; if so, return its copy. Otherwise, create a new vertex copy and store it in the table. Recursively copy each neighbor and append it to the new vertex's neighbor collection.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Every vertex and edge is visited once. Space is consumed by the lookup registry and traversal call stack.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing without caching existing copies leads to infinite recursion on cycles and duplicated vertex copies.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A hash mapping from old node to new node ensures exactly V allocations and O(1) duplicate checks.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling null graph, cycle prevention using a map, deep copying all neighbor connections rather than referencing originals.
